blocks.text: ORI:100–122 DETAILED REVIEW AND DELEGATED APPROVAL — CANONICAL

This block was reconsidered from first principles under delegated approval authority. The review compared five genuinely different candidate directions per root (45 candidates total), recorded 360 criterion scores, ran 114 concept and boundary stress tests, passed 18 canonical packet checks, and preserved every deterministic generated form.

Approved architecture: ORI:1xx is the Origin process layer for bounded ontological transitions. The inward triplet owns source-ground establishment; the outward triplet owns distinct actualization; the systemic triplet owns shared-world transition. Their third-trit contrast is completed, active, and nonactualized.
ORI:100 — completed source-ground establishment — Completion of a bounded ontological transition by which one referent becomes grounded as a source from which another state of affairs may originate.
ORI:101 — active source-ground establishment — An ongoing bounded ontological transition by which one referent is becoming grounded as a source from which another state of affairs may originate.
ORI:102 — nonactualized source-ground establishment — A nonactualized bounded ontological transition that would ground one referent as a source from which another state of affairs may originate.
ORI:110 — completed distinct actualization — Completion of a bounded ontological transition by which one distinct referent comes to obtain as part of the relevant reality.
ORI:111 — active distinct actualization — An ongoing bounded ontological transition by which one distinct referent is coming to obtain as part of the relevant reality.
ORI:112 — nonactualized distinct actualization — A nonactualized bounded ontological transition by which one distinct referent would come to obtain as part of the relevant reality.
ORI:120 — completed shared-world transition — Completion of a bounded ontological transition by which what obtains across one shared reality changes under one jointly applicable world condition.
ORI:121 — active shared-world transition — An ongoing bounded ontological transition by which what obtains across one shared reality is changing under one jointly applicable world condition.

ORI:122 — nonactualized shared-world transition — A nonactualized bounded ontological transition by which what obtains across one shared reality would change under one jointly applicable world condition.

Design boundary: these roots do not silently encode causation, time or scheduling, observation, representation, truth, physical mechanics, production, or modality. Lexical nonactualization does not itself mean possible, intended, prepared, scheduled, or future. Runtime [2]/num remains assertion-level uncertainty and does not select a third-trit-2 lexical root.
